mbm-1326.clue: I chase trains with a box of crayons.
mbm-1326.quote: My nephew picks a crayon before the local comes into view. If it matches an engine stripe, we both draw the train. On the day he picked pink we had to wait for sunset.

mbm-1327.clue: I turned the last hole into a bakery.
mbm-1327.quote: I built my own little putting course from cereal boxes and a rolling pin. At the final hole you putt through a model bakery door. I made a tiny loaf for the winner.

mbm-1328.clue: I cut the stars before the night.
mbm-1328.quote: For the courtyard party I folded dark blue papel picado and cut a field of little stars. One corner tore off. I left the gap exactly as it was and called it the comet.

mbm-1329.clue: I keep the sound effects in a shoebox.
mbm-1329.quote: At anime club we turn down the volume and invent the sounds ourselves. My tin of dry beans does a convincing space engine until somebody mistakes it for a snack.

mbm-1330.clue: My puppet has two different slippers.
mbm-1330.quote: I ran out of purple silk halfway through my little glove-puppet baker’s costume. I gave him one green slipper and a backstory about dressing before dawn. The kids always check his feet.

mbm-1331.clue: I was the doorbell for three weeks.
mbm-1331.quote: The stage doorbell broke during our village play. I stood behind the scenery with a teaspoon and a little brass bowl. Actors began waiting for my second note before they opened the door.

mbm-1332.clue: I bring a postcard to the campsite.
mbm-1332.quote: My friend and I set a postcard of last year’s camp against a stone. We pitch the tent on the same spot and see what’s changed. One tiny sapling has grown to cover half the old view.

mbm-1333.clue: I know where the loud water goes quiet.
mbm-1333.quote: Our raft came through choppy water and slipped behind a big rock into a still pocket. All I could hear was my friend catching her breath. Then we looked at each other and laughed into the quiet.

mbm-1334.clue: I leave the secret in the sugar bowl.
mbm-1334.quote: I make a white cube vanish under a napkin at family breakfast. My little brother always checks the sugar bowl first, so last Sunday I put a tiny paper flag in there to congratulate him on his investigation.

mbm-1335.clue: I draw the wake from the dock.
mbm-1335.quote: After water skiing I sit with a pencil and try to catch the crossing lines the boat leaves behind. My dad hangs the best drawings upside down. He says they look like mountains that way.

mbm-1336.clue: I planted a garden beside the robot.
mbm-1336.quote: I built a giant green mecha and set a tiny row of carrot tops at its feet. My sister painted the shovel in its hand. Our family calls it the most expensive gardener in the neighborhood.

mbm-1337.clue: I put the old wizard in retirement.
mbm-1337.quote: The sleeve on my oldest fantasy card is worn clear at the corners. I built the wizard a little paper armchair by the deck box. He watches my matches with a cup of tea drawn beside him.

mbm-1338.clue: I tie a ribbon where I turn around.
mbm-1338.quote: I run out along the orchard lane with a red ribbon in my pocket. At the halfway tree I tie it to a low branch, circle the pond and collect it on the way home. The route feels like unwrapping a present.

mbm-1339.clue: I made a dish for exactly three cherries.
mbm-1339.quote: I pressed three little hollows into a clay leaf before it dried. At breakfast my niece fills each with a cherry, then eats them in order from stalk to tip. Apparently the leaf has rules.

mbm-1340.clue: I wrote a program that loses its hat.
mbm-1340.quote: My tiny screen character tips his hat each time the clock strikes. One wrong number sent his hat sailing off the screen. I added a little breeze and kept the mistake for windy afternoons.

mbm-1341.clue: I can find my lane by the music.
mbm-1341.quote: The ball return at our alley rattles in a three-note rhythm. I tap it on my leg between shots. When I took Mum bowling she said she’d been hearing that tune at our kitchen table for years.

mbm-1342.clue: I made a deck for the storm.
mbm-1342.quote: I chose every fantasy card in my deck just because it had a cloud in the picture. I lost my first five matches. On the sixth, all that ridiculous rain actually put out the dragon.

mbm-1343.clue: I gave my model a ladder to nowhere.
mbm-1343.quote: I attached a tiny ladder to the outside of my mecha’s hangar before I’d designed the roof. I put a little lookout chair at the top. The mechanic up there now has the best view on the shelf.

mbm-1344.clue: I made a skirt from two different nights.
mbm-1344.quote: Two old dance skirts were each too torn to wear. I joined the good half of the blue one to the good half of the green. When I turn in the mirror they make a third color in the middle.

mbm-1345.clue: I put my old gym key on a ribbon.
mbm-1345.quote: The first weight room I joined has closed. I tie its brass key to my current locker knob while I train. One hard-earned habit travels perfectly well from room to room.

mbm-1346.clue: I ski past the snowman twice.
mbm-1346.quote: A child built a little snowman low beside the beginner slope. On the first run I gave him a pinecone nose, and on the second a pinecone friend. Soon everyone on the lift was checking how he was doing.

mbm-1347.clue: I listen for the kettle halfway through the story.
mbm-1347.quote: We hang the camp kettle just beside the fire when someone starts a tale. Whoever is speaking when it whistles pours the cocoa. I save my best pauses for just before the whistle.

mbm-1348.clue: I bring a fan made from a map.
mbm-1348.quote: I folded an old city map into a hand fan for sunny afternoons. From my deck chair I can still pick out the street where I grew up. It happens to be on the breeziest fold.

mbm-1349.clue: I have rules about the last biscuit.
mbm-1349.quote: On our pajama comedy nights the last biscuit goes to the first person who can repeat the funniest line without laughing. It often survives the whole episode and most of the credits.

mbm-1350.clue: I point the camera at the listeners.
mbm-1350.quote: At family parties I photograph the person hearing a story instead of the person telling it. My favorite print shows my uncle’s mouth just beginning to smile, a full second before the punch line.
